roll.roll_source_note: recording | procedural. recording = ONE car-level layer (loop + band-pass hiss + tread-block tone) on the sealed surfaces below; procedural = the per-wheel filtered-noise roll (always the fallback, and used on unsealed surfaces)
roll.status: PROVISIONAL: AI-generated recording (owner, 2026-10-18), sounds like distant highway-rest-stop traffic roll, not a close tyre; recording speed unknown, rate_reference_speed_kmh is [AS]. Levels/laws rewritten 2026-10-19 (owner: the tyre noise switched on below 50 km/h and then stayed the same in level and pitch).
roll.level_note: gain = gain_at_reference * (v / reference_speed)^(level_db_per_decade / 20), v clamped at max_speed. level_db_per_decade 35 [AS]: CPX/CPB tyre/road noise follows 30-40 dB per decade of speed on dense surfaces (Sandberg & Ejsmont, Tyre/Road Noise Reference Book, Informex 2002; CNOSSOS-EU rolling-noise coefficient 30 for light vehicles). Before 2026-10-19: exponent 1 (20 dB per decade) clamped at 200 km/h.
roll.max_speed_note: far above the hypercar's 446 km/h top speed; the law keeps growing up to here
roll.rate_note: playback rate of the recording = (v / rate_reference_speed)^rate_exponent: the rolling-noise spectrum shifts up slowly with speed. Before: clamp(v / 50 km/h, 0.5, 2.0) = frozen pitch below 25 and above 100 km/h.
roll.hiss_note: band-pass noise, centre at the reference speed 1 kHz (tread impact / air pumping peak 0.8-1.2 kHz), rising with v^0.3; dB relative to the recording's RMS
roll.tone_note: tread-block passing frequency = tread speed / pitch = blocks per revolution x wheel revolutions per second (0.032 m = about 62 blocks round a 2.0 m circumference [AS]); follows the wheels' angular speed, not the chassis

surfaces.surfaces_note: sealed = uses the car-level layer; db = level offset re dense asphalt [AS] (Sandberg & Ejsmont ch. 4: tined concrete +2..4, pavers +4..7, setts/cobbles +6..10 dB; soft ground quieter). Names not listed here are unsealed at 0 dB.
